conditions: Record must be an issue that has a parent issue set (i.e., it is a sub-issue, not top-level)
The candidate's direct parent issue must currently have Maya Chen as its assignee
There must be exactly one issue satisfying both of the above, since the request uses the singular 'the sub-issue'
The action is to set the priority field of that sub-issue (not its parent) to the 'High' level

records.note: WEB-1 'Checkout redesign' has no parentId, so it is not a sub-issue at all. It is itself assigned to Maya Chen, but that's irrelevant since the request needs a sub-issue whose *parent* is assigned to Maya.
WEB-2 has parentId i-31, and i-31's assignee is u-maya (Maya Chen). It is the only sub-issue meeting both r1 and r2, so r3 (uniqueness) also holds. This is the correct target for r4.
WEB-3 'Cart improvements' has no parentId, so it fails r1 outright; it is itself assigned to Sam Rivera, not relevant to Maya at all.

WEB-4 has parentId i-33, satisfying r1, but i-33's assignee is u-sam (Sam Rivera), not Maya Chen. Notably i-34 itself is assigned to Maya Chen — a classic near-miss confusing the sub-issue's own assignee with its parent's assignee. A careful reader rejects this since the request is explicit that the *parent* must be assigned to Maya.

turn2.differences: None. The author's four conditions match my step-1 reading exactly: sub-issue status (parentId present), parent's assignee = Maya Chen, uniqueness implied by the definite singular 'the sub-issue', and the update action applying to the sub-issue itself rather than its parent.
turn2.naturalness_note: The phrasing is a little more formally precise ('whose parent issue is assigned to') than casual speech, but this is plausible language for a Linear user describing an issue-hierarchy relationship; nothing about it signals an artificial test scenario.
